#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release drift check (gh-2042, AC2): re-download every `fa-*` asset of a
# release and diff sha256 against the signed SHA256SUMS.
#
# The v1.0.680 incident: assets were re-attached to the published release
# ~2-3h AFTER the manifest was signed, so the manifest no longer described
# the shipped bytes and every `fa update` / install.sh provenance check on
# the train failed. This is the CI-side twin of bin/self_manage.dart's
# verifyReleaseProvenance — same manifest, same digest comparison — run
# after every release publish and on a schedule
# (.github/workflows/release-drift-watch.yml). Drift = red run + a details
# file the remediation step pages from + an auto re-request of
# release-provenance. Drift must page, not linger.
#
# Checks (any hit = drift, exit 1):
#   - SHA256SUMS / SHA256SUMS.sig present on the release (no signature = no
#     provenance at all — the SEC-07 #795 fail-closed class);
#   - every manifest entry's digest matches the downloaded bytes
#     (sha256sum -c);
#   - the manifest covers EXACTLY the release's fa-* set (an fa-* asset on
#     the release that the manifest does not list is a stale manifest — the
#     v1.0.680 `-mac.zip` shape; a manifest entry the release no longer
#     serves is a missing asset — the gh-1832 shape).
#
# Usage: release_drift_check.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN,
#      FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR (tests only: verify a pre-populated directory
#      instead of downloading), FA_DRIFT_DETAILS (drift details file, the
#      remediation step pages from it; default drift-details.txt in the CWD).
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_drift_check.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
details="${FA_DRIFT_DETAILS:-drift-details.txt}"

drift=()
report() { # report <line>: collects the drift finding + names it in the details file
  drift+=("$1")
  printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$details"
}

workdir="${FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR:-$(mktemp -d)}"
if [ -z "${FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR:-}" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$workdir"
  # The manifest and its signature ride their own pattern: `fa-*` does not
  # match them, and BOTH must be on the release for provenance to exist.
  gh release download "$tag" --repo "$repo" --dir "$workdir" --pattern 'fa-*'
  gh release download "$tag" --repo "$repo" --dir "$workdir" --pattern 'SHA256SUMS*' || true
fi

rm -f "$details"

if [ ! -f "$workdir/SHA256SUMS" ]; then
  report "SHA256SUMS is NOT on release $tag — provenance can never be verified (SEC-07 #795 fail-closed class)"
else
  if [ ! -f "$workdir/SHA256SUMS.sig" ]; then
    report "SHA256SUMS.sig is NOT on release $tag — an unsigned manifest is not provenance"
  fi
  if ! (cd "$workdir" && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS > "$workdir/sha-check.log" 2>&1); then
    while IFS= read -r line; do
      case "$line" in
        *FAILED*|*failed*)
          report "digest drift: $line"
          ;;
      esac
    done < "$workdir/sha-check.log"
  fi
fi

# Set diff, both directions: the manifest must cover EXACTLY the fa-* set
# actually on the release.
manifest_names=$(sed -n 's/^[0-9a-fA-F]\{64\}[[:space:]]\+\*\?//p' "$workdir/SHA256SUMS" 2>/dev/null || true)
local_names=$(find "$workdir" -maxdepth 1 -name 'fa-*' -type f -printf '%f\n' 2>/dev/null | sort)
unlisted=$(comm -23 <(printf '%s\n' "$local_names" | sort -u) <(printf '%s\n' "$manifest_names" | sort -u) | sed '/^$/d')
uncovered=$(comm -13 <(printf '%s\n' "$local_names" | sort -u) <(printf '%s\n' "$manifest_names" | sort -u) | sed '/^$/d')
for name in $unlisted; do
  report "stale manifest: fa asset $name is on the release but NOT in SHA256SUMS (attached after signing?)"
done
for name in $uncovered; do
  report "missing asset: SHA256SUMS lists $name but the release no longer serves it (gh-1832 shape)"
done

if [ "${#drift[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "drift-details file: $details" >&2
  for line in "${drift[@]}"; do
    echo "::error::release drift on $tag: $line (gh-2042 AC2 — the signed SHA256SUMS no longer matches the shipped assets; remediation: re-run release-provenance for the tag)" >&2
  done
  exit 1
fi

echo "✅ release drift check passed for $tag: every fa-* asset matches the signed SHA256SUMS ($(printf '%s\n' "$local_names" | grep -c . || true) assets)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release drift remediation (gh-2042, AC2): when the drift check finds a
# published release whose assets no longer match the signed SHA256SUMS, this
# step (a) auto re-requests the release-provenance job for the tag — the job
# re-hashes the CURRENT assets and re-signs the manifest, which is also the
# AC3 v1.0.680 remediation mechanism — and (b) pages a DEDUPLICATED issue so
# drift never lingers silently.
#
# The re-request targets the SIGN JOB (`gh run rerun --job`), never the
# whole tag run: a full rerun would rebuild + re-attach every asset, which
# the immutability gate (scripts/release_asset_gate.sh, gh-2042 AC1) now
# refuses on a published release — and a rebuild is not what remediation
# needs anyway (the shipped bytes are the truth; only the manifest is stale).
#
# Paging FIRST-CLASS: the issue is filed even when the re-request fails or
# the tag run cannot be found (deleted history, PR-only branch names) — the
# only total failure of this step is the issue filing itself failing.
#
# Issue dedup: exact title `[release-drift] SHA256SUMS drift on <tag>` —
# an open match gets a comment (a fresh data point), never a duplicate.
#
# Usage: release_drift_remediate.sh <tag> <drift-details-file>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_drift_remediate.sh <tag> <drift-details-file>}"
details_file="${2:?usage: release_drift_remediate.sh <tag> <drift-details-file>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"

details="(drift details unavailable)"
[ -f "$details_file" ] && details=$(cat "$details_file")

rerun_status="(re-request not possible: no completed workflow run found for tag $tag on ci.yml)"
# `// 0` (not `// ""`): jq encodes the empty STRING as `""` — with quotes —
# which would defeat the emptiness guard. 0 is never a real run id.
run_id=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml --branch "$tag" \
  --limit 30 --json databaseId,conclusion \
  --jq '[.[] | select(.conclusion != null)] | first | .databaseId // 0' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
if [ "$run_id" != "0" ] && [ -n "$run_id" ]; then
  job_id=$(gh api "repos/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id/jobs" --paginate \
    --jq '.jobs[] | select(.name == "Sign release checksums") | .id' 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "${job_id:-}" ]; then
    if gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --job "$job_id" 2>/dev/null; then
      rerun_status="release-provenance re-requested: run $run_id, job $job_id (it re-hashes the current assets and re-signs — gh-2042 AC2/AC3)"
    else
      rerun_status="re-request FAILED: gh run rerun $run_id --job $job_id was rejected — rerun the 'Sign release checksums' job manually"
    fi
  else
    rerun_status="re-request FAILED: no 'Sign release checksums' job on run $run_id — rerun release-provenance for the tag manually"
  fi
fi

title="[release-drift] SHA256SUMS drift on $tag"
body="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/release-drift-body.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$body"' EXIT
{
  echo "## $title"
  echo
  echo "$details"
  echo
  echo "**Auto-remediation (gh-2042 AC2):** $rerun_status"
  echo
  echo "If the drift persists after the re-run, an attach path replaced fa-* assets on the published release again — find it and gate it (scripts/release_asset_gate.sh). Until the manifest matches the shipped bytes, \`fa update\` / install.sh provenance verification fails for this train."
} > "$body"

# Dedup: exact open-title match (the inject-failure verify pattern) →
# comment; otherwise create. Best-effort label so the issues are filterable.
existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --limit 200 \
  --json number,title --jq '.[] | select(.title == $t) | .number' --arg t "$title" 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)
if [ -n "$existing" ]; then

    || { echo "::error::drift on $tag: could not comment the open drift issue #$existing — page the release owner manually" >&2; exit 1; }

else
  gh label create release-drift --repo "$repo" --color D97706 --description "Published release assets drifted from the signed SHA256SUMS" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  gh issue create --repo "$repo" --title "$title" --label release-drift \
    --body-file "$body" >/dev/null \
    || { echo "::error::drift on $tag: could not file the drift issue — page the release owner manually" >&2; exit 1; }
  echo "✅ drift issue filed for $tag — paged (gh-2042 AC2: drift must not linger)"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release asset immutability gate (gh-2042, AC1): the single attach path for
# `fa-*` assets onto a GitHub Release.
#
# The v1.0.680 incident: the daily build-macos train resolved a tag whose
# release was ALREADY PUBLISHED (the same-tag convergence race — the tag
# train published while the daily train's slow self-hosted legs were still
# building) and re-attached fresh fa-macos-arm64 assets ~2-3h AFTER the
# signed SHA256SUMS was attached. The manifest never re-ran, so every
# `fa update` / install.sh provenance check on the train failed for every
# macOS-arm64 user. A published release must be IMMUTABLE for `fa-*`
# assets: the signed manifest vouches for exactly the bytes that were on
# the release when release-provenance signed it.
#
# Verdicts (per call, all-or-nothing — a partial attach would still drift
# the manifest):
#   release missing        → allow (the caller lazy-drafts first; a raw
#                            upload to a missing release errors loudly)
#   release is a DRAFT     → attach everything --clobber (the gh-1801 flow,
#                            unchanged: publish stays provenance-owned)
#   release is PUBLISHED   → for every listed asset:
#                              - name already attached → immutable SKIP
#                                (the release-twin binaries re-run: same
#                                tag commit, asset already shipped)
#                              - name not attached, matches `fa-*` →
#                                REFUSE the whole call with a loud
#                                ::error:: (post-publish attach must
#                                target a DRAFT / next-version or re-run
#                                release-provenance for the tag)
#                              - name not attached, NOT fa-* → attach
#                                (store AAB/IPA/APK + DMG refreshers are
#                                deliberately not provenance-covered,
#                                see scripts/release_required_assets.txt)
#   anything undeterminable (API blip, unparseable verdict) → fail CLOSED
#
# SHA256SUMS(.sig) are NOT fa-* assets: release-provenance's raw
# `gh release upload` of the manifest is the sanctioned post-publish
# remediation (re-hash the current bytes, re-sign) and stays outside this
# gate by design (gh-2042 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_asset_gate.sh <tag> <asset> [<asset>...]
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_asset_gate.sh <tag> <assets...>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
shift
assets=("$@")
if [ "${#assets[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "::error::release_asset_gate.sh called with zero assets for $tag — a caller bug: resolve at least one artifact or skip the release step" >&2
  exit 1
fi

err=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$err"' EXIT
state_json=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json isDraft,assets 2>"$err") || {
  if grep -qi "not found" "$err"; then
    # Release absent: the attach path lazily creates the DRAFT first
    # (release_lazy_draft.sh / the create in release_attach_or_create.sh).
    # Attempt the upload — a still-missing release errors loudly in gh.
    for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
      gh release upload "$tag" "$asset" --clobber --repo "$repo"
    done
    echo "✅ gate: release $tag absent — attached ${#assets[@]} asset(s) (draft-first flow)"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "::error::cannot determine the release state of $tag ($(cat "$err")) — refusing to attach (gh-2042 fail-closed: an undeterminable verdict must never mutate a release)" >&2
  exit 1
}

if printf '%s' "$state_json" | jq -e '.isDraft == false' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # PUBLISHED — the immutability contract.
  attached=$(printf '%s' "$state_json" | jq -r '.assets[].name')
  refused=()
  skipped=()
  uploadable=()
  for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
    name=$(basename "$asset")
    if printf '%s\n' "$attached" | grep -qxF "$name"; then
      skipped+=("$name")
    elif [[ "$name" == fa-* ]]; then
      refused+=("$name")
    else
      uploadable+=("$asset")
    fi
  done
  if [ "${#refused[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "::error::release $tag is PUBLISHED — attaching unattached fa-* asset(s) [${refused[*]}] would invalidate its signed SHA256SUMS (gh-2042 AC1: a published release is immutable for fa-* assets). Remediate by re-running the release-provenance job for the tag (it re-hashes the current assets and re-signs), or target the next-version DRAFT instead." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  for name in "${skipped[@]:-}"; do
    [ -n "$name" ] || continue
    echo "✅ gate: $name already on the published release $tag — immutable skip (gh-2042)"
  done
  for asset in "${uploadable[@]:-}"; do
    [ -n "$asset" ] || continue
    gh release upload "$tag" "$asset" --clobber --repo "$repo"
    echo "✅ gate: $(basename "$asset") attached to $tag (not provenance-covered)"
  done
  exit 0
fi

if printf '%s' "$state_json" | jq -e '.isDraft == true' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # DRAFT — the normal pre-publish attach (unchanged since gh-1801).
  for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
    gh release upload "$tag" "$asset" --clobber --repo "$repo"
  done
  echo "✅ gate: ${#assets[@]} asset(s) attached to draft $tag — publish stays provenance-owned"
  exit 0
fi

echo "::error::unparseable release state for $tag — refusing to attach (gh-2042 fail-closed)" >&2
exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Attach assets to <tag>'s release, creating it when missing — the single
# draft-capable create path for build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# (issue #282 E3 + review of #294).
#
# Race-idempotent (E3): if `gh release create` loses the view→create race
# (another job/run created the release in between), fall back to
# uploading into the winner's release instead of failing. A failed create
# would fire the job's draft lifecycle guard against the WINNER's
# in-flight draft.
#
# Ownership-stamped: the create path makes a DRAFT (gh-1801 rework: the
# release never goes live from a leg — the tag-run release-provenance job
# publishes + flags latest once the signed SHA256SUMS is attached). The
# body stamps
#   <!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job_id> -->
# and release_draft_guard.sh deletes that draft ONLY on an exact
# run+job match — never the sibling leg's mid-upload draft (daily-publish
# runs the mobile and macOS legs concurrently on the same derived tag).
# The marker is an invisible HTML comment in the body.
#
# Usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <asset> [<asset>...]
#   reads the release body from release-notes.md in the CWD (a minimal
#   body is written when the file is missing/empty)
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <assets...>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
shift
assets=("$@")
if [ "${#assets[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  # gh-1801 hard refusal: creating a release with zero resolved assets is
  # the `fa update` breaker (an empty `latest` 404s every
  # fa-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz until backfill — v1.0.630, 2026-10-23). Attaching
  # is the caller's only honest option when it resolved nothing — fail
  # loud here, never create empty. Pinned by
  # test/release_empty_latest_guard_test.dart.
  echo "::error::no assets to attach for $tag — refusing to create or touch a release with an empty asset list (gh-1801): resolve at least one artifact or skip the release step" >&2
  exit 1
fi

upload_all() { # exists-path: gate-guarded attach + (servable DRAFT-only) publish + latest
  # gh-2042 (AC1): every upload passes the immutability gate — on a
  # PUBLISHED release an unattached fa-* asset refuses the whole call loud,
  # an already-attached one skips, and non-fa store/DMG refreshers keep
  # their clobber-refresh contract. Drafts attach exactly as before.
  for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
    bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_asset_gate.sh" "$tag" "$asset"
  done
  # Latest policy (#282 + gh-1801 rework + gh-2042): publish + latest ONLY
  # when the release can actually serve `fa update` — that means the signed
  # checksums are already on it (`fa update` hard-fails without
  # SHA256SUMS(.sig), bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate) — AND it is
  # still a DRAFT (the provenance-flip recovery window). A PUBLISHED
  # release is never re-flaged `--latest` here: on an older release that
  # would drag the latest badge (and `fa update`) backwards to a downgrade.
  if release_serves_fa_update; then
    case "$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft 2>/dev/null || echo false)" in
      true)
        gh release edit "$tag" --draft=false --latest --repo "$repo"
        # gh-1899: same duplicate-tag race as the tag train — a twin draft
        # minted by a sibling leg of THIS run would otherwise rot until the
        # 24h sweeper. The tag is published and servable here (the flip is
        # gated on the signed checksums), so own-run twin drafts are orphans.
        bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_draft_dedupe.sh" "$tag" \
          || echo "::warning::gh-1899 twin-draft dedupe failed — the release is published and servable, so this is cleanup noise only; the 24h sweeper remains the backstop"
        ;;
      *)
        echo "release $tag is already published — publish/latest flip skipped (gh-2042: latest never moves backwards; the signed SHA256SUMS re-upload is release-provenance's job)"
        ;;
    esac
  else
    echo "release $tag is not yet servable (no SHA256SUMS on it) — publish+latest left to the release-provenance step (gh-1801)"
  fi
}

# fa-update servability = the signed checksums are on the release. Every
# fa-* archive alone is NOT enough: `fa update` fetches SHA256SUMS(.sig)
# and aborts when either is missing (bin/self_manage.dart).
release_serves_fa_update() {
  local names
  names=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json assets --jq '.assets[].name' 2>/dev/null || true)
  printf '%s\n' "$names" | grep -qE '^SHA256SUMS(\.sig)?$'
}

if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  upload_all
  echo "✅ attached ${#assets[@]} asset(s) to existing release $tag"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: prepared notes (CHANGELOG section / conventional-commit fallback)
# plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
notes="release-notes.md"
marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)} -->"
[ -s "$notes" ] || printf 'Release %s — see the CHANGELOG.\n' "$tag" > "$notes"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >> "$notes"

# A `gh release create` for a MISSING tag mints a lightweight API tag:
# no push event → no ci.yml tag run → no publish/binaries (the v0.1.408
# silent class, issue #597). If the ref is absent, mint it as an
# ANNOTATED tag and push it with the PAT the job already carries
# (GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT in build-macos) so the tag CI fires. The mint
# itself (GH_TOKEN guard, persisted-checkout-extraheader strip, push,
# train-start verification) lives in scripts/release_tag_mint.sh —
# gh-2026: the v1.0.663 / v1.0.665 minted pushes rode actions/checkout's
# persisted GITHUB_TOKEN extraheader (it outranks the URL credentials),
# GitHub suppresses workflow triggers for GITHUB_TOKEN pushes, no tag run
# ever existed on those refs, and the drafts rotted behind green legs.
# A mint whose train does not start now fails loud BEFORE any draft is
# created, so the leg goes red and the failure-path draft guard has
# nothing to reclaim.
# Gate on the DEFINITE missing verdict (ls-remote --exit-code rc 2):
# sandboxes without an origin remote fatal with 128 — indeterminable
# falls through to the plain create path (test fixtures rely on it).
set +e
git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1
ls_remote_rc=$?
set -e
if [ "$ls_remote_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_tag_mint.sh" "$tag"
fi

# Bare vX.Y.Z title (#282): matches the tag, matches pub.dev. gh-1801
# rework: the create is DRAFT-ONLY. Whatever this leg resolved
# (AAB/IPA/store APKs, DMGs/zips) is not the signed provenance `fa update`
# demands — a leg that arrives first must never publish the release, let
# alone flag it latest (threads 2/6). The draft is ownership-stamped (the
# marker below) so this job's draft lifecycle guard reclaims it on
# failure; the tag-run binaries job attaches the CLI assets into it and
# release-provenance (ci.yml) publishes + flags latest once SHA256SUMS.sig
# is on board.
if gh release create "$tag" \
  --repo "$repo" \
  --title "$tag" \
  --draft \
  --notes-file "$notes" \
  "${assets[@]}"; then
  echo "✅ created draft release $tag with ${#assets[@]} asset(s) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"
  exit 0
fi

# E3 idempotency: the create may have lost the view→create race — the
# winner's release now exists. Attach instead of failing (a failing
# create would fire the guard against the winner's in-flight draft).
if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  upload_all
  echo "✅ lost the create race — attached ${#assets[@]} asset(s) to the concurrently created release $tag"
  exit 0
fi

echo "::error::release create for $tag failed and no concurrent release appeared — see the step log above" >&2
exit 1

# gh-2042 — release drift watch (AC2 + the AC3 remediation vehicle).
#
# The v1.0.680 incident: assets were re-attached to the ALREADY-PUBLISHED
# release ~2-3h after the signed SHA256SUMS was attached; the manifest never
# re-ran and every `fa update` provenance check on the train failed for
# macOS-arm64. The attach paths are now gated
# (scripts/release_asset_gate.sh, gh-2042 AC1) — this workflow is the
# detection backstop for ANY drift that still reaches a published release:
#
#   - after every release publish (the `release: published` event fires when
#     release-provenance flips the draft — the manifest is on board by then):
#     verify the tag's shipped bytes against its signed SHA256SUMS;
#   - on a DAILY schedule: the same check for the latest published release
#     (the one `fa update` serves) — drift must page, not linger;
#   - on demand (workflow_dispatch with a tag): the manual remediation
#     vehicle — dispatching it for v1.0.680 IS the AC3 remediation: the
#     check detects the stale manifest and the remediation step auto
#     re-requests the release-provenance job, which re-hashes the CURRENT
#     assets and re-signs.
#
# On drift the run goes red, a deduplicated issue pages the owner, and the
# "Sign release checksums" job of the tag's ci.yml run is re-requested
# (scripts/release_drift_remediate.sh — job-scoped rerun, never a full run:
# a full rerun would rebuild + re-attach, which the AC1 gate refuses on a
# published release).
name: Release drift watch

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Daily, offset from the other crons (ci 23 */2, daily-publish 17 5,
    # nightly 17 3 / 17 7).
    - cron: '51 6 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: 'Tag to verify (empty = the latest published release). Dispatch for a stale-manifest tag IS the provenance re-sign remediation (gh-2042 AC3).'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# SEC-08: explicit minimal default — the job declares its own block below.
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: release-drift-watch
  cancel-in-progress: false # a drift check is never preempted mid-page

jobs:
  drift-watch:
    name: Verify assets match the signed SHA256SUMS
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read # download the release assets
      actions: write # re-request the release-provenance job on drift
      issues: write # the deduplicated drift page
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Resolve target release
        id: target
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "${{ inputs.tag }}" ]; then
            tag="${{ inputs.tag }}"
            echo "source=dispatch"
          elif [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "release" ]; then
            tag="${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}"
            echo "source=release event"
          else
            tag=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name)
            echo "source=schedule (latest published)"
          fi
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "verifying $tag"

      - name: Verify assets against the signed manifest (gh-2042 AC2)
        run: bash scripts/release_drift_check.sh "${{ steps.target.outputs.tag }}"

      - name: Page + auto re-request release-provenance (drift never lingers)
        if: failure()
        run: |
          bash scripts/release_drift_remediate.sh \
            "${{ steps.target.outputs.tag }}" \
            drift-details.txt

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG (`scripts/auto_release.sh`
  via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main (gh-1522: the retired flow
  pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit per release). gh-1801: NO
  GitHub Release is created at tag-cut time (an asset-less create
  published an empty `latest` that broke `fa update`): the tag-run
  `binaries` job creates the release DRAFT-first via
  `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh` (curated CHANGELOG notes via
  `release_notes.sh` + a `release-draft-owner` marker), every leg attaches
  into it, and `release-provenance` publishes + flags `latest` ONLY after
  the signed SHA256SUMS(.sig) is attached — `latest` never points at a
  release that cannot serve `fa update`. The git TAG is the single source
  of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` + `release-provenance`
  jobs (the release publishes at the provenance step). `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- Lockfile policy (gh-1296 NG1): EVERY lockfile is committed and enforced —
  one inventory list in `scripts/check_lockfiles.sh` (7 files:
  `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `ios/Podfile.lock`, `macos/Podfile.lock`,
  the vendored `flutter_inappwebview_macos` `Package.resolved`, both e2e
  `package-lock.json`s, and `vendor/wasm_run/native/Cargo.lock`); a listed
  lockfile that is missing/untracked/gitignored fails the Static gates, and
  pod-sync (flutter-analyze + nightly build legs, after `pub get`) fails
  when a native iOS/macOS plugin resolved by pubspec.lock has no pod in the
  platform's `Podfile.lock` (the gh-1274 class), or its pod is pinned at a
  stale version vs the resolved plugin podspec's `s.version` (the
  historical flutter_gemma 1.8.0-vs-1.11.3 skew; the podspec is the comparison target,
  not the pubspec version — vendored/beta pods legitimately differ from the
  Dart package version). The inventory also enforces the gh-1303 path-pin
  sync: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` pins this repo as a path dependency, so
  its `flutter_agent_harness` pin must EXIST and equal the root
  `pubspec.yaml` version — a stale OR MISSING pin (e.g. a merge conflict
  resolved by dropping the entry) makes every
  `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` consumer red — the pins are
  `0.0.0-dev` on both sides and NEVER churn across releases (gh-1522: the
  tag is the version; the release flow mutates zero files), and the Static
  gate catches any other path to the drift at PR time. After ANY pubspec.yaml
  dependency change that adds/updates a darwin-native plugin: `cd
  flutter_app/ios && pod install --repo-update` and the same in `macos/`,
  commit both `Podfile.lock`s (CocoaPods runs fine on Linux for
  regeneration; the wasm_run `nm` step needs an llvm-nm shim + the
  XCFramework staged via `scripts/setup_vendor_ios.sh` or the upstream zip).
  Guard red exits are fixture-self-tested (`scripts/
  check_lockfiles_selftest.sh`, Static gates).
- TestFlight external distribution (issue #239): the `submit_only` lanes
  (driven by build-mobile.yml / build-macos.yml) distribute every build
  straight to the EXTERNAL group — REQUIRED repo variables
  `TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP`, `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL`,
  `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE`, `BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL` (lanes fail loudly
  at start without them). Pilot must WAIT for processing (skipping the wait
  silently skips distribution); `verify_external_distribution!` asserts
  group membership bounded — beta-review-pending is a neutral notice, a
  build never reaching the group fails the leg (self-filed issue).
- Manual App Store review: `release-appstore.yml` (workflow_dispatch:
  `version` + `platforms` ios/macos/both + `confirm` repeating the version)
  runs the `submit_for_review` lanes — pure pre-flight in
  `flutter_app/fastlane/appstore_preflight.rb` (plain-ruby tested) fails
  BEFORE any mutation; already-submitted versions are a green no-op;
  release-after-approval stays a manual ASC click
  (`APP_STORE_AUTOMATIC_RELEASE` repo variable flips it, E5). Grep-guards:
  `test/store_automation_guard_test.dart`.
- App Store content pipeline (no binary): store screenshots are COMMITTED
  goldens from `flutter_app/test/golden/store_screenshots_test.dart` (frame +
  inline en/ru copy in `store_marketing_frame.dart`) at
  `flutter_app/test/goldens/store/{en,ru}/{ios,ipad,mac}/` — regenerate with
  `flutter test test/golden/store_screenshots_test.dart --update-goldens`,
  then open every PNG. Store copy lives in
  `flutter_app/fastlane/metadata/{ios,macos}/{en-US,ru-RU}/` (the lanes strip
  name.txt/subtitle.txt — App Info is not editable post-release); release
  notes come from the latest `## […]` section of
  `store_artefacts/metadata/{en,ru}/changelog.md`. Upload: `fastlane ios
  app_store` / `fastlane mac app_store` in `flutter_app` (env gates
  `IOS_DEPLOY_METADATA`/`IOS_DEPLOY_SCREENSHOTS`/`MACOS_DEPLOY_*`; ASC API key
  env secrets) or the `store-metadata.yml` workflow (`ios_content`/
  `macos_content` inputs: none/metadata_only/screenshots_only/all).
- Google Play listing pipeline (issue #289, no binary): the Play Console
  image rules are repo tests. Listing screenshots are the same story frames
  as COMMITTED GOLDENS straight into the supply tree
  (`fastlane/metadata/android/{en-US,ru-RU}/images/`): phone 1080×1920
  (exact 9:16, en+ru), 10-inch 1440×2560 (exact 9:16 — 1600×2560 is 10:16
  and Play rejects it; en only, ru falls back to phone shots), regenerated
  with `flutter test test/golden/store_screenshots_test.dart
  --update-goldens` then `git checkout -- test/goldens/store` (the run also
  refreshes the App Store goldens on a non-canonical host — restore them);
  the feature graphic (1024×500) is a widget golden in
  `test/golden/play_store_assets_test.dart`; the icon is the iOS master
  resized by `tool/generate_android_adaptive_icons.dart` (512×512, mirrored
  byte-identical to ru-RU). Sizes/aspects/file caps are enforced by
  `flutter_app/test/play_store_listing_guard_test.dart`. Listing texts
  (title ≤30, short_description ≤80, full_description) live in
  `fastlane/metadata/android/{en-US,ru-RU}/`. Upload: `fastlane android
  play_store` in `flutter_app` (env gates `PLAY_DEPLOY_METADATA`/
  `PLAY_DEPLOY_IMAGES`, `PLAY_VALIDATE_ONLY=1` dry-run; Play service-account
  secret `PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON`) or the `store-metadata.yml`
  android leg (`android_content`: none/metadata_only/images_only/all). Images
  never ride supply (it only APPENDS uploads — issue #947): the `play_store`
  lane pushes them through `play_listing_sync.rb`, which replaces the whole
  image set per locale + device type (dropped sets are cleared) and verifies
  the committed goldens against `edits.images.list`. The daily
  `daily-publish.yml` play leg dispatches `build-mobile.yml` with
  `android_content=all`, so every release train redeploys the listing.

gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            provenance/SHA256SUMS provenance/SHA256SUMS.sig \
            --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          # gh-1801 (rework): THE publish point of the train. The release
          # now carries every fa-* asset AND the signed SHA256SUMS(.sig) —
          # the first moment `fa update` can actually serve it (it
          # hard-fails without the signed checksums, bin/self_manage.dart).
          # Flip draft=false + latest here and ONLY here: a red provenance
          # leaves the previous release as latest (safe degradation)
          # instead of stranding a provenance-less one (the v1.0.630
          # empty/partial-latest window class).
          #
          # gh-2042 (BLOCKING review thread): the flip must never drag the
          # `latest` badge backwards. The drift remediation
          # (scripts/release_drift_remediate.sh) re-requests THIS job for
          # an old drifted tag; a job rerun re-executes this step with the
          # original run's ref, and an unconditional --latest would
          # re-flag that older release as Latest — pointing every
          # `fa update` client DOWN at it (the re-signed manifest would
          # make the downgrade pass provenance). Carry --latest ONLY when
          # the release is still a draft (the normal publish point,
          # gh-1801) or already the current latest; otherwise publish the
          # re-signed state without touching the badge.
          is_draft=$(gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft)
          current_latest=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name 2>/dev/null || true)
          if [ "$is_draft" = "true" ] || [ "$current_latest" = "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" ]; then
            gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          else
            # Re-sign remediation of a non-latest tag: publish state is
            # already correct — never drag the latest badge backwards
            # (gh-2042).
            gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          fi

  # invocation would judge each asset against its own release-view

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release drift check (gh-2042, AC2): ...
# (header additions: GNU-bound note; infra-vs-drift note)
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_drift_check.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
details="${FA_DRIFT_DETAILS:-drift-details.txt}"

drift=()
report() {
 drift+=("$1")
 printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$details"
}

# gh-2042 review (suggestion): the details reset runs BEFORE any download
# — a check that dies mid-download must never leave stale content for the
# remediation step to page as if it were today's drift.
rm -f "$details"

workdir="${FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR:-$(mktemp -d)}"

# gh-2042 review (suggestion): transient transport blips are NOT drift
# evidence. Retry once; treat ONLY an explicit not-found/no-match verdict
# as a deterministic "absent" (rc 2). Any other failure after the retry is
# infra (rc 1) → the step fails WITHOUT a drift page (the next scheduled
# run re-checks); the workflow's remediation step pages only when a
# non-empty details file exists.
gh_dl() { # gh_dl <pattern> → 0 downloaded, 2 deterministic absent, 1 infra
 local pattern="$1" attempt err rc
 for attempt in 1 2; do
   err=$(mktemp)
   rc=0
   gh release download "$tag" --repo "$repo" --dir "$workdir" --pattern "$pattern" 2>"$err" || rc=$?
   if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
     rm -f "$err"
     return 0
   fi
   if grep -Eqi 'not found|no assets match' "$err"; then
     rm -f "$err"
     return 2
   fi
   rm -f "$err"
   [ "$attempt" -lt 2 ] && sleep "${FA_DRIFT_RETRY_SLEEP:-2}"
 done
 return 1
}

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release drift check (gh-2042, AC2): re-download every `fa-*` asset of a
# release and diff sha256 against the signed SHA256SUMS.
#
# The v1.0.680 incident: assets were re-attached to the published release
# ~2-3h AFTER the manifest was signed, so the manifest no longer described
# the shipped bytes and every `fa update` / install.sh provenance check on
# the train failed. This is the CI-side twin of bin/self_manage.dart's
# verifyReleaseProvenance — same manifest, same digest comparison — run
# after every release publish and on a schedule
# (.github/workflows/release-drift-watch.yml). Drift = red run + a details
# file the remediation step pages from + an auto re-request of
# release-provenance. Drift must page, not linger.
#
# Checks (any hit = drift, exit 1):
#   - SHA256SUMS / SHA256SUMS.sig present on the release (no signature = no
#     provenance at all — the SEC-07 #795 fail-closed class);
#   - every manifest entry's digest matches the downloaded bytes
#     (sha256sum -c);
#   - the manifest covers EXACTLY the release's fa-* set (an fa-* asset on
#     the release that the manifest does not list is a stale manifest — the
#     v1.0.680 `-mac.zip` shape; a manifest entry the release no longer
#     serves is a missing asset — the gh-1832 shape).
#
# Exit codes (gh-2042 review: infra is NOT drift evidence):
#   0  clean — every fa-* asset matches the signed SHA256SUMS;
#   1  DRIFT — a verdict a human must see (the workflow pages from the
#      details file + auto re-requests release-provenance);
#   2  INFRA — the assets could not be downloaded (transport error after a
#      retry): red run, but NO drift page (the next scheduled run
#      re-checks; the remediation step only pages on a non-empty details
#      file, which an infra failure never writes).
#
# Usage: release_drift_check.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN,
#      FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR (tests only: verify a pre-populated directory
#      instead of downloading), FA_DRIFT_DETAILS (drift details file, the
#      remediation step pages from it; default drift-details.txt in the CWD),
#      FA_DRIFT_RETRY_SLEEP (seconds between download retries; default 2).
#
# GNU-bound (sha256sum -c, find -printf, comm): this check targets the
# ubuntu-latest workflow runner — it fails confusingly if run locally on
# macOS/BSD.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_drift_check.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
details="${FA_DRIFT_DETAILS:-drift-details.txt}"

drift=()
report() { # report <line>: collects the drift finding + names it in the details file
  drift+=("$1")
  printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$details"
}

# The details reset runs BEFORE any download (gh-2042 review): a check that
# dies mid-download must never leave stale checkout content behind for the
# remediation step to page as if it were today's drift.
rm -f "$details"

workdir="${FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR:-$(mktemp -d)}"

# Download with a transient-blip guard (gh-2042 review): retry once on
# transport failures (502, rate limit, ...) and treat ONLY an explicit
# not-found / no-match verdict as a deterministic "absent" (rc 2). Any
# other failure after the retry is infra (rc 1).
gh_dl() { # gh_dl <pattern> → 0 downloaded, 2 deterministic absent, 1 infra
  local pattern="$1" attempt err rc
  for attempt in 1 2; do
    err=$(mktemp)
    rc=0
    gh release download "$tag" --repo "$repo" --dir "$workdir" --pattern "$pattern" 2>"$err" || rc=$?
    if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
      rm -f "$err"
      return 0
    fi
    if grep -Eqi 'not found|no assets match' "$err"; then
      rm -f "$err"
      return 2
    fi
    rm -f "$err"
    if [ "$attempt" -lt 2 ]; then
      sleep "${FA_DRIFT_RETRY_SLEEP:-2}"
    fi
  done
  return 1
}

if [ -z "${FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR:-}" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$workdir"
  # The manifest and its signature ride their own pattern: `fa-*` does not
  # match them, and BOTH must be on the release for provenance to exist.
  fa_rc=0
  sha_rc=0
  gh_dl 'fa-*' || fa_rc=$?
  gh_dl 'SHA256SUMS*' || sha_rc=$?
  if [ "$fa_rc" -eq 1 ] || [ "$sha_rc" -eq 1 ]; then
    echo "::error::release drift check could not download the assets of $tag (transport error after retry) — an infra blip is NOT drift evidence: failing WITHOUT a drift page; the next scheduled run re-checks" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
fi

if [ ! -f "$workdir/SHA256SUMS" ]; then
  report "SHA256SUMS is NOT on release $tag — provenance can never be verified (SEC-07 #795 fail-closed class)"
else
  if [ ! -f "$workdir/SHA256SUMS.sig" ]; then
    report "SHA256SUMS.sig is NOT on release $tag — an unsigned manifest is not provenance"
  fi
  if ! (cd "$workdir" && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS > "$workdir/sha-check.log" 2>&1); then
    while IFS= read -r line; do
      case "$line" in
        *FAILED*|*failed*)
          report "digest drift: $line"
          ;;
      esac
    done < "$workdir/sha-check.log"
  fi
fi

# Set diff, both directions: the manifest must cover EXACTLY the fa-* set
# actually on the release. The names are read LINE-WISE (gh-2042 review):
# release asset names may contain spaces, and a word-split loop would
# report one bogus per-word "asset" instead of the whole name.
manifest_names=$(sed -n 's/^[0-9a-fA-F]\{64\}[[:space:]]\+\*\?//p' "$workdir/SHA256SUMS" 2>/dev/null || true)
local_names=$(find "$workdir" -maxdepth 1 -name 'fa-*' -type f -printf '%f\n' 2>/dev/null | sort)
unlisted=$(comm -23 <(printf '%s\n' "$local_names" | sort -u) <(printf '%s\n' "$manifest_names" | sort -u) | sed '/^$/d')
uncovered=$(comm -13 <(printf '%s\n' "$local_names" | sort -u) <(printf '%s\n' "$manifest_names" | sort -u) | sed '/^$/d')
while IFS= read -r name; do
  [ -n "$name" ] || continue
  report "stale manifest: fa asset $name is on the release but NOT in SHA256SUMS (attached after signing?)"
done <<< "$unlisted"
while IFS= read -r name; do
  [ -n "$name" ] || continue
  report "missing asset: SHA256SUMS lists $name but the release no longer serves it (gh-1832 shape)"
done <<< "$uncovered"

if [ "${#drift[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "drift-details file: $details" >&2
  for line in "${drift[@]}"; do
    echo "::error::release drift on $tag: $line (gh-2042 AC2 — the signed SHA256SUMS no longer matches the shipped assets; remediation: re-run release-provenance for the tag)" >&2
  done
  exit 1
fi

echo "✅ release drift check passed for $tag: every fa-* asset matches the signed SHA256SUMS ($(printf '%s\n' "$local_names" | grep -c . || true) assets)"

- name: Resolve target release
        id: target

          # gh-2042 review: untrusted template values ride env-var
          # indirection, never direct ${{ }} interpolation into the run:
          # shell (the GitHub Actions security-hardening guide's script

        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "$DISPATCH_TAG" ]; then
            tag="$DISPATCH_TAG"
            echo "source=dispatch"
          elif [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "release" ]; then
            tag="$RELEASE_EVENT_TAG"
            echo "source=release event"
          else
            tag=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name)
            echo "source=schedule (latest published)"
          fi
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  bogus per-word findings) and the header documents the GNU-bound tools.

  exit 2 + no page, 404→drift verdict), spaced-asset-name tests, GNU
  note pin, env-indirection + details-gate workflow lints." && git log --oneline -1

**Fixed** in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` ("Upload provenance assets" step, ci.yml:4515 area).

The reviewer's suggested shape is applied verbatim: the flip is now conditional —

```bash
is_draft=$(gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft)
current_latest=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ "$is_draft" = "true" ] || [ "$current_latest" = "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" ]; then
  gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
else
  # Re-sign remediation of a non-latest tag: publish state is already
  # correct — never drag the latest badge backwards (gh-2042).
  gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
fi
```

So a job rerun for an old drifted tag (exactly what `release_drift_remediate.sh` re-requests) re-publishes the corrected manifest **without** `--latest` — the `latest` badge can no longer move backwards, and the fleet-wide `fa update` downgrade path is closed. The normal publish point (draft flip, gh-1801) and the AC4 pins are unchanged.

Pinned by `test/release_drift_workflow_test.dart` → *"the provenance flip never drags `latest` backwards (gh-2042 BLOCKING review thread)"*: the step must gate `--latest` on `isDraft` + `releases/latest`, must carry a `--draft=false --repo` fallback without `--latest`, and must name gh-2042.

The `.github/workflows/release-drift-watch.yml` header comment now also documents the guarded flip (dispatching drift-watch for an older tag re-signs without dragging the badge).

# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6ypRMY` — transient blips indistinguishable from drift

**Fixed** in `scripts/release_drift_check.sh` (+ the workflow's remediation step) with the suggested "distinguish 404 from transport errors, retry once" design:

- New `gh_dl` helper wraps both `gh release download` calls (`fa-*` and `SHA256SUMS*`): retry once on failure (backoff `FA_DRIFT_RETRY_SLEEP`, default 2 s), and treat **only** an explicit `not found` / `no assets match` stderr verdict as a deterministic "absent". The old asymmetric paths are gone — no more swallowed `|| true` on the manifest download and no more unguarded `fa-*` download.
- Persistent transport failure after the retry exits **2** with a `::error::` naming the transport class and writes **no** drift details file: an infra blip is not drift evidence. The `.github/workflows/release-drift-watch.yml` "Page + auto re-request" step now pages **only** when `drift-details.txt` is non-empty (`[ -s drift-details.txt ]`); otherwise it stays silent (red run, no issue, no provenance re-request) — the next scheduled run re-checks.
- A 404-class verdict keeps its deterministic meaning: the check proceeds and reports the real drift verdict (e.g. *"SHA256SUMS is NOT on release"* → exit 1 + details → page), as the reviewer intended.
- Bonus from the same thread's hazard note: the `rm -f "$details"` reset moved **before** the downloads, so an early death never leaves stale checkout content to page under the real-drift dedup title.

Pinned by three stubbed-`gh` behavioral tests in `test/release_drift_check_test.dart` (blip-then-success → exit 0 with exactly one retry; persistent blip → exit 2, no details file, one retry; `release not found` → exit 1 + the missing-manifest drift verdict) and by the workflow lint *"the remediation step pages ONLY on a non-empty drift details file"*. All verified RED against the pre-fix script.

# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6ypRPM` — unquoted set-diff expansion breaks on names with spaces

**Fixed** in `scripts/release_drift_check.sh` with the suggested line-wise reads:

```bash
while IFS= read -r name; do
  [ -n "$name" ] || continue
  report "stale manifest: fa asset $name is on the release but NOT in SHA256SUMS (attached after signing?)"
done <<< "$unlisted"
```

(same shape for the `$uncovered` / missing-asset loop). A spaced asset name now lands in ONE report line instead of splitting into bogus per-word "assets".

The header also gained the requested GNU-bound note: *GNU-bound (`sha256sum -c`, `find -printf`, `comm`): this check targets the ubuntu-latest workflow runner — it fails confusingly if run locally on macOS/BSD.*

Pinned by two tests in `test/release_drift_check_test.dart`: *"asset names with spaces are reported whole"* (a `fa-macos arm64.tar.gz` on the release but not in the manifest must be reported as the full name — RED against the word-splitting loop) and *"a manifest-covered asset with spaces verifies clean"* (the whole-line manifest/set-diff match on the happy path).

arguments.content:
## Issues/Notes

- **Owned CI violations: none.** `ci_failures.md` at rework start reports *no failed checks* (no "Violations you must fix" table) — all CI was green on the rework head; no `disputed` items.
- **Review decision `NONE`, 7 open review threads** (1 BLOCKING, 4 IMPORTANT, 2 SUGGESTION) — **all 7 addressed with code fixes in this pass**, each verified TDD-style (regression test RED before the fix, GREEN after; noted per thread below).
- The two committed test-run residue files (`release-notes.md`, `drift-details.txt`) were the visible symptom of a test-hermeticity gap — both the symptom and the root cause are fixed.
- A `bash_job` background full-suite run covers the regression check (`dart test --exclude-tags integration,browser-ext,llm,pty`); branch-push validation CI remains the authoritative full-suite gate (per repo convention the 4 pre-existing `test/integration/` PTY/yolo reds are environment-bound and untouched by this change).

## Approach

1. **BLOCKING — the `--latest` downgrade path closed at the flip itself** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, "Upload provenance assets"): the publish flip is now conditional — `--latest` only when the release is still a **draft** (the gh-1801 publish point) or is **already the current latest**; any other (published, non-latest) tag — exactly the shape a `release_drift_remediate.sh` job-rerun produces — publishes the re-signed state **without** `--latest`. Re-signing an old tag can no longer drag the `latest` badge (and `fa update`) backwards onto it. The drift-watch workflow header documents the guarded AC3 dispatch.
2. **Residue + hermeticity**: deleted `drift-details.txt` + `release-notes.md` from the branch, gitignored both (CWD artifacts of the release scripts), and removed the generator: `_runCheck` in `test/release_drift_check_test.dart` pins `FA_DRIFT_DETAILS` inside the fixture temp dir; `release_drift_check.sh` also resets the details file **before** any download so an early death never leaves stale content to page.
3. **Shell-injection hardening** (`.github/workflows/release-drift-watch.yml`): `inputs.tag`, `github.event.release.tag_name` and `steps.target.outputs.tag` ride `env:` indirection into the `run:` shells (`DISPATCH_TAG` / `RELEASE_EVENT_TAG` / `TAG`); no untrusted `${{ }}` remains interpolated in any `run:` block.
4. **All-or-nothing gate restored**: `release_attach_or_create.sh` passes the **whole asset list to one `release_asset_gate.sh` call** (was once-per-asset), so the documented per-call refuse-before-upload contract actually holds in production — one state snapshot, no partial mutation, no N× API round-trips.
5. **Infra ≠ drift** (`release_drift_check.sh`): downloads retry once; only an explicit `not found`/`no assets match` verdict is deterministic absence; a persistent transport failure exits **2** and writes no drift details — and the drift-watch remediation step pages **only** on a non-empty details file, so a runner blip can no longer file a false drift incident (red run, silent page path, next schedule re-checks).
6. **Line-wise set-diff**: the unlisted/uncovered loops read `comm` output with `while IFS= read -r` (spaced asset names stay whole instead of word-splitting into bogus findings); the header documents the GNU-bound tooling.
7. Every fix followed RED→GREEN: the regression tests were written first and confirmed failing against the reviewed code (details in `outputs/review_replies/*.md`), then the minimal change turned them green; scripts pass `bash -n`; changed Dart files are `dart format`-clean.

## Files Modified

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — conditional provenance flip (no `--latest` on a non-latest published tag; the BLOCKING thread).
- `.github/workflows/release-drift-watch.yml` — env-var indirection for untrusted template values; `TAG` passed to check/remediate steps; remediation pages only on a non-empty drift-details file; header comments updated (guarded flip, silent-infra path).
- `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh` — one gate call for the whole asset list.
- `scripts/release_drift_check.sh` — `gh_dl` retry/not-found helper, infra exit 2 without a drift page, details reset before downloads, line-wise set-diff loops, GNU-bound header note.
- `.gitignore` — `/release-notes.md`, `/drift-details.txt` (script CWD artifacts).

You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see the TDD approach section included later in this prompt — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix

content.text:
permissions:
      contents: read # download the release assets
      actions: write # re-request the release-provenance job on drift
      issues: write # the deduplicated drift page
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Resolve target release
        id: target
        env:
          # gh-2042 review: untrusted template values ride env-var
          # indirection, never direct ${{ }} interpolation into the run:
          # shell (the GitHub Actions security-hardening guide's script
          # injection pattern — this job holds actions:write + issues:write).
          DISPATCH_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
          RELEASE_EVENT_TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "$DISPATCH_TAG" ]; then
            tag="$DISPATCH_TAG"
            echo "source=dispatch"
          elif [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "release" ]; then
            tag="$RELEASE_EVENT_TAG"
            echo "source=release event"
          else
            tag=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name)
            echo "source=schedule (latest published)"
          fi
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "verifying $tag"

      - name: Verify assets against the signed manifest (gh-2042 AC2)
        env:
          TAG: ${{ steps.target.outputs.tag }}
          FA_DRIFT_DETAILS: drift-details.txt
        run: bash scripts/release_drift_check.sh "$TAG"

      - name: Page + auto re-request release-provenance (drift never lingers)
        if: failure()
        env:
          TAG: ${{ steps.target.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-2042 review: only DRIFT pages. A transport/infra failure
          # exits the check red WITHOUT writing the details file — the run
          # stays red but files no issue and re-requests nothing (the next
          # scheduled run re-checks; the release's provenance is intact).
          if [ -s drift-details.txt ]; then
            bash scripts/release_drift_remediate.sh "$TAG" drift-details.txt
          else
            echo "red WITHOUT drift details — transport/infra failure, not drift: no page, no re-request (the next scheduled run re-checks)"
          fi

- **CHANGED** (0): _none_
- **UNCHANGED** (0): _none_

## New Comments & Review Threads (17)

### 1. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-11-02:97c54786` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-11-02

🚨 **BLOCKING: the AC3 remediation vehicle re-flags an old release `--latest` — a fleet-wide `fa update` downgrade**

The remediation chain this PR wires up can move the `latest` badge **backwards**, which the PR itself declares must never happen:

1. `scripts/release_drift_remediate.sh:43` re-requests the tag's **"Sign release checksums"** job:
   ```bash
   gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --job "$job_id"
   ```
2. That job's "Upload provenance assets" step ends with an **unconditional** flip (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:4515`):
   ```bash
   gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
   ```
   A job rerun re-executes **all** its steps with the original run's ref, so `GITHUB_REF_NAME` is the (possibly old) tag.
3. `gh release edit --latest` is "**Explicitly mark the release as 'Latest'**" (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_release_edit) — it designates that release as Latest *regardless of whether a newer release exists*.
4. The new workflow explicitly advertises the dangerous path as its primary use (`.github/workflows/release-drift-watch.yml:16`): *"dispatching it for v1.0.680 IS the AC3 remediation"*. Once any newer release exists, dispatching drift-watch for an older drifted tag re-flags that older release as Latest → every `fa update` client "updates" **down** to it (the re-signed manifest makes the downgrade pass provenance verification).

The PR's own invariant text: *"A PUBLISHED release is never re-flaged `--latest` here: on an older release that would drag the latest badge (and `fa update`) backwards to a downgrade"* (`scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh:57-58`, same wording in `test/release_publish_imutability_test.dart:10`). The attach path enforces it; the remediation path reintroduces it.

Note the scheduled/`release: published` paths are safe (they only ever target the current latest), so this bites exactly the documented manual-remediation flow.

**Suggested fix** — make the flip conditional in the provenance job (keeps the gh-1801 publish point and the AC4 pin intact):

```bash
is_draft=$(gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft)
is_latest=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ "$is_draft" = "true" ] || [ "$is_latest" = "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" ]; then
  gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
else
  # Re-sign remediation of a non-latest tag: publish state is already
  # correct — never drag the latest badge backwards (gh-2042).
  gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
fi
```

### 2. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-11-02:ce8065df` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-11-02

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: committed test-run residue files (`release-notes.md`, `drift-details.txt`)**

Both new root files are artifacts of running the new scripts with **fixture** values — `v1.2.3`, `run/111/job/binaries-linux-arm64` and `fa-windows-x64.zip` exist only in the test fixtures:

- `release-notes.md` — the minimal fallback body + draft-owner marker written by `release_attach_or_create.sh` when invoked from the repo root (the current-run marker would be appended on top of the stale one).
- `drift-details.txt` — the drift check's default `FA_DRIFT_DETAILS` output, containing fake findings ("digest drift: fa-windows-x64.zip: FAILED open or read").

This is verifiably residue, not intentional fixtures: running the PR's own verify command regenerates `drift-details.txt` **byte-identical** at the repo root (verified during this review — the tracked file changes on every `dart test` run).

Functional hazard beyond hygiene: the drift-watch workflow pages from `drift-details.txt` in the checkout root. `release_drift_check.sh` only resets that file (`rm -f "$details"`) **after** the downloads, so if the check dies early (e.g. a transient `gh release download` failure — the `fa-*` download at line 47 has no `|| true`), the "Page + auto re-request" step files a GitHub issue quoting this stale committed content as if it were today's drift — a false incident page with fabricated data.

**Fix**: delete both files from the branch and add `drift-details.txt` / `release-notes.md` to `.gitignore` (both are CWD artifacts of the release scripts — nothing on `main` tracks them today).

### 3. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-11-02:2924b285` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-11-02

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `_runCheck` writes the drift details file into the repo root on every test run**

`_runCheck` (lines 46-61) sets `FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR` but not `FA_DRIFT_DETAILS`, so every *failing* check in this suite (tampered, unlisted, no-manifest, no-sig, missing-asset) writes `drift-details.txt` into the `dart test` CWD — the **repo root**. After this PR that path is a tracked file, so the suite dirties the checkout on every run; this is exactly how the committed `drift-details.txt` residue (see the other thread) got created — my verification run reproduced it byte-identically.

**Fix** — keep the seam hermetic:

```dart
], environment: {
  'GITHUB_REPOSITORY': 'OWNER/REPO',
  'GH_TOKEN': 'stub',
  'FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR': dir.path,
  'FA_DRIFT_DETAILS': '${dir.path}/details.txt',
});
```

(The one test that exercises the details file already does this correctly — line 154+.) Alternatively default the script's `details` to `$workdir/drift-details.txt` instead of CWD-relative, but then `release-drift-watch.yml` must pass/export the same path explicitly so the remediation step still finds the file.

### 4. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-11-02:3f6ce02e` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-11-02

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: untrusted `${{ }}` interpolation into `run:` shell — use env indirection**

The "Resolve target release" step interpolates `${{ inputs.tag }}` and `${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}` directly into a `run:` block:

```yaml
if [ -n "${{ inputs.tag }}" ]; then
  tag="${{ inputs.tag }}"
```

and the resolved value is then re-interpolated in the two downstream `run:` steps as `"${{ steps.target.outputs.tag }}"`. This is the classic GitHub Actions script-injection pattern: a tag value containing shell metacharacters (`` ` ``, `$( )`, `;`) executes in the runner — a job holding `contents: read` + `actions: write` + `issues: write`.

Both `workflow_dispatch` and release publishing currently require repo write access, so this is not an external-attacker path — but it is exactly the hazard class this repo's SEC-08 posture (explicit least-privilege blocks in this very workflow) works to avoid, and GitHub's security-hardening guide calls for env-var indirection for *all* untrusted template values.

**Fix**:

```yaml
- name: Resolve target release
  id: target
  env:
    DISPATCH_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
    RELEASE_EVENT_TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
  run: |
    set -euo pipefail
    if [ -n "$DISPATCH_TAG" ]; then
      tag="$DISPATCH_TAG"
    elif [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "release" ]; then
      tag="$RELEASE_EVENT_TAG"
    ...
```

and pass the result into the check/remediate steps the same way (`env: TAG: ${{ steps.target.outputs.tag }}` → `"$TAG"`). Repo precedent exists both ways (`release-appstore.yml` interpolates inputs directly — equally flaggable), so this is hardening-for-consistency, not a regression unique to this PR.
